articles.title: 2 dead, 11 injured after Kansas mother drives onto soccer field during game: Police
articles.summary: Police said the driver of the truck is a 34-year-old mother.
articles.body:
Two people, including a 6-year-old boy, were killed and 11 others injured after a truck drove through a youth soccer game in Wichita, Kansas, on Saturday afternoon, police said, in what officials called a "heartbreaking" incident that authorities are still investigating.

First responders rushed to Stryker Soccer Complex after receiving multiple 911 calls around 3:25 p.m. CT, Capt. Aaron Moses of the Wichita Police Department told reporters at a press conference Saturday evening.

Police said the driver, who they identified only as a 34-year-old woman of Garden City, Kansas, stayed with the truck after the incident.

"She has been cooperative to this point in the investigation," he said, adding later she was in police custody.

Moses told reporters he believed one of the driver's children was playing soccer at the complex on Saturday but was not on that field at the time of the incident.

There were two juveniles who were also inside the truck at the time it went onto the field, police said.

When police arrived at the scene, the truck was located on the west end of the field and bystanders were helping to render aid to the injured people on the field, Moses said.

The two people who died -- a 6-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man, both of McPherson, Kansas -- were pronounced dead on the scene, police said.

Of the 11 people who were injured and taken to the hospital, five are children, ranging in age from 5 to 9.

The injured adults range in age from 28 to 68.

Of the injured, 10 had "traumatic injuries," Moses said, saying they ranged from bruises to "extremely severe injuries."

Police stressed they are still investigating and asked the public for patience.

"We know what happened, but now we're working very hard to find out why it happened, and we're not there yet," Wichita Police Chief Joe Sullivan told reporters.

Police said they have interviewed over 30 witnesses at the scene and are asking anyone with pictures or video of the incident to share them with investigators.

Police also credited bystanders who the police chief said "sprang into action so quickly and gave life-saving assistance until the arrival of first responders." Sullivan added, "It was truly amazing, but I think it's indicative of the of the Wichita community."

Wichita Mayor Lily Wu said "Tonight, Wichita grieves together."

"Today is a heartbreaking day for Wichita," Mayor Lily Wu told reporters. "Families came to Stryker Sports Complex to enjoy a Saturday afternoon watching their children play soccer. No one could have imagined the tragedy that would unfold."

The city of Wichita said in a Facebook post Saturday afternoon that all events at the sports complex have been canceled until further notice.

"We ask that you keep all individuals and families affected in your thoughts and prayers during this difficult time," the city said in a statement.

Kansas Gov. Laura Kelly said in a statement she was monitoring the situation and in touch with the mayor.

"My condolences go out to the families of the victims, the survivors, and all those impacted by this event," Kelly said in a statement.

In a statement, the Stryker Soccer Complex said it was praying for those affected.

"Our hearts are heavy as we process the tragic events at Stryker today," the statement said. "We are holding everyone impacted, the injured, their families, and all those who witnessed this heartbreaking event close in our thoughts and prayers."

ABC News' Chris Barry, Brianna Sanchez and Michael Pappano contributed to this report.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

Former Vanderbilt standout quarterback Diego Pavia was in attendance to watch Colorado and head coach Deion Sanders take on No. 11 Utah at Folsom Field on Saturday night.

The 24-year-old served as Vanderbilt's starting quarterback in 2025, throwing for 3,539 yards and 29 touchdowns while finishing No. 2 in Heisman Trophy voting. Pavia then signed with the Baltimore Ravens as an undrafted free agent, but was waived before the start of the 2026 season.

articles.title: Rays Beat Guardians in Game 4 to Even ALCS, Box Score Stats, Highlights, Updated MLB Playoff Bracket
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays evened the American League Championship Series at two games apiece with a 7-3 win over the Cleveland Guardians on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays evened the American League Championship Series at two games apiece with a 7-3 win over the Cleveland Guardians on Saturday.

A two-RBI play from Jonathan Aranda in the seventh following a fielding error paired with a two-run homer from Yandy Díaz in the top of the ninth helped seal the win for the Rays.

The victory moves the Rays one step closer to their first World Series appearance since 2020, when they fell to the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Ahead of Game 4, Tampa Bay entered as a 1.5-point favorite over Cleveland, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , and delivered on expectations with a statement road win.

The Guardians and Rays split the first two games at Tropicana Field in Florida, with Cleveland taking Game 1, 7-3, before Tampa Bay responded with a 3-1 win in Game 2.

After the series shifted to Progressive Field, Cleveland capitalized on home-field advantage to win Game 3 and take a 2-1 series lead. Tampa Bay answered in Game 4, earning a road win to even the series and set up what is sure to be an exciting ALCS.

No. 4 New York Yankees def. No. 5 Boston Red Sox, 2-0

No. 3 Atlanta Braves def. No. 6 Philadelphia Phillies, 2-1

The Guardians felt the home crowd on Sunday, striking first in the bottom of the first on a Chase DeLauter single to right field that brought home Steven Kwan from second base for Cleveland to take a 1-0 lead.

Tampa Bay's Aranda answered in the third with an RBI single, bringing home Díaz, who had doubled, to even the score at 1-1.

The Rays tacked on another run in the top of the sixth, with Junior Caminero doubling to bring home Jonathan Aranda and give Tampa Bay a 2-1 lead.

A huge seventh inning proved to be the difference for Tampa Bay, as the Rays scored three runs to take a commanding 5-1 lead on the road.

After two players stole bases to move into scoring position, Aranda hit a single that turned into a two-RBI play following a fielding error by Cleveland's DeLauter, allowing Aranda to advance to third base.

Chandler Simpson followed with a sacrifice fly to bring Aranda home as the Rays began to pull away.

Guardians' Travis Bazzana launched a solo home run in an attempt to keep Cleveland within striking distance, scoring the team's first run since the opening inning.

Cleveland kept the momentum going, with Brayan Rocchio delivering an RBI to cut Tampa Bay's lead to 5-3 in the bottom of the seventh.

Díaz hit a two-run homer to bring home Richie Palacios in the top of the ninth, adding an insurance run as Tampa Bay took a 7-3 lead that held through the final out.

The series will remain in Cleveland for Game 5, scheduled for Sunday, with first pitch set for 5 p.m. ET.

Manchester United visit Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday afternoon on six points from six league games, without a win in their last four league matches.

They drew 1-1 at home to Tottenham Hotspur, who had Rodrigo Bentancur sent off, then lost 2-0 at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday, conceding after 53 seconds and finishing with 10 men after Leny Yoro was sent off. United have not won any of their four away games this season, and Leeds beat them 2-1 at Old Trafford in April.

Benjamin Sesko (shin) is out, with Carrick saying he is still a little further away and needs more checks. Patrick Dorgu (hamstring), Tom Heaton (abdominals) and Manuel Ugarte (ACL) are also out. Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo missed the Atletico game through injury and will face late fitness tests, and Noussair Mazraoui has only recently returned to training. Matthijs de Ligt is back in contention after almost a year out with a back problem.

Lisandro Martinez, who criticised the club's technical director Jason Wilcox after the Atletico defeat, has been confirmed in the squad by Carrick and could start alongside Harry Maguire. If Shaw is not fit, Diogo Dalot is likely at left-back with Yoro on the right. Carlos Baleba may make his first Premier League start alongside Youri Tielemans if Mainoo is unavailable. Bruno Fernandes is expected at number 10 behind Bryan Mbeumo, with Amad Diallo and Matheus Cunha either side.

articles.title: Man United players suspect unexpected factor is behind disastrous form, it’s not Carrick or Wilcox
articles.summary: Manchester United were expected to challenge for major trophies this season after securing a third-place finish in the Premier League.Six games into the new...
articles.body:
Manchester United were expected to challenge for major trophies this season after securing a third-place finish in the Premier League.

Six games into the new campaign, the Red Devils sit 14th in the table and have already been knocked out of the Carabao Cup.

Michael Carrick has received criticism for his failure to properly work on his side's physicality and intensity over the summer. Meanwhile, Jason Wilcox has come under fire for not addressing glaring issues in the squad during the transfer window.

However, some United stars believe there may be another reason to blame for their poor run of form.

Manchester United stars fear documentary is reason for disastrous start

Amazon Prime's popular fly-on-the-wall sporting series All or Nothing is focusing on Manchester United this season.

According to The Sun , United stars fear documentary cameras are affecting their season "because staff and players are holding their tongue in post-match debriefs."

It is claimed players believe the cameras "stifle dressing-room chat during and after games, to the detriment of performances."

A source told The Sun: "The players view the cameras as a pain.

"They not only have to meet with them every couple of weeks to do filming, they think that having them in the dressing room means the players and the managers aren't being as open as they could be about what has been going wrong and what needs to be done to fix it.

"Some of the players are more keen on it than others but the ones that don't like them think punches are being pulled in the wake of games."

It is difficult to determine the true impact of cameras in and around the dressing room when it comes to United's performances.

However, United's antics on the field must have already generated a lot of nail-biting content for Amazon.

Most recently, Lisandro Martinez took aim at Wilcox for his frustrating work in the transfer market following the Red Devils' defeat against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. Needless to say, his comments would have invited some heated reaction in the dressing room as well.

Furthermore, Michael Carrick may find himself on the chopping block if results do not improve. Another managerial change would create even more dramatic events for Amazon cameras to record.

articles.title: Oklahoma fans meltdown as Kentucky knocks off Sooners; they also booed injured Nic Anderson in classless act
articles.summary: Kentucky knocked off the Sooners, and fans are melting down. They earned it after a classless act toward Nic Anderson.
articles.body:
For a 3rd straight time, Kentucky Football invaded an opposing SEC city and came away with the W. This time, the Cats left a bunch of crying Oklahoma fans in their wake.

Many fans are simply ready for the entire coaching staff to be fired:

Oklahoma fans also looked really bad during the game when they booed former Sooners wideout Nic Anderson as he was walking off the field with an injury. Completely classless, both by fans at the game and on Twitter.

When you are going on the road and have every fanbase upset by the end of the night, you are doing things right. Speaking of the fans, they were turning on each other too.

When are people going to realize that Will Stein has Kentucky on another level? This is not the old Kentucky that is coming in hoping to keep it close. This is a Kentucky team coming for the throat each and every time they are on the field.

Losing to Kentucky is not a bad loss, folks. It may even get to a point where a win against Kentucky is a quality win. Even sad Texas fans found a little solace in Kentucky's ability to knock off the Sooners.

Kentucky is now in a bowl game for the first time in 3 seasons. But they may skip the entire bowl season and jump in the CFP. Speaking of which, how cool is it to see the CFP official X account post about Kentucky?

There are still some really tough games to go, but the Cats could theoretically drop one of those and still find themselves in the College Football Playoff.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Experts Top 25 Rankings After Week 7
articles.summary: Chaos. Absolute chaos.
articles.body:
The No. 1 (Georgia), No. 2 (Notre Dame), No. 4 (Indiana), No. 5 (Alabama) and No. 8 (Texas) teams in last week's B/R Top 25 all lost on Saturday, and three other ranked teams outside the top 10 fell, paving the way for a complete top-to-bottom shuffling of this week's Top 25.

Suddenly, multiple two-loss SEC teams fit comfortably into the national picture, while multiple Big 12 undefeateds fit prominently into the preliminary College Football Playoff picture now that Week 7 is in the books.

There is still a lot of football to be played, and Saturday proved that the championship conversation is truly wide open heading into the second half of the season.

Ahead is an updated look at how the college football experts here at B/R line up the nation's top 25 teams following Week 7 action.

Note: Rankings will be updated as needed once late games go final.

Week 7 Result: WIN at Georgia (27-24) Next Week: vs. LSU

The Tigers got to two losses faster than some other SEC teams, but following their victory over No. 1 Georgia and zooming out on a resume whose blemishes are losses to Florida and Tennessee by a combined 14 points, their outlook has changed. Dual-threat quarterback Byrum Brown had 150 passing yards, 115 rushing yards and two touchdowns, the Tigers won the turnover battle (3-0) and Alex McPherson drilled the game-winning 34-yard field goal as time expired.

24. Northwestern (5-1, Previous Rank: NR)

Week 7 Result: WIN at Michigan State (24-21) Next Week: vs. Rutgers

The Wildcats trailed 21-13 with 11:48 remaining in the fourth quarter following a Michigan State touchdown, but they responded with a nine-play, 77-yard touchdown drive of their own and successful two-point conversion to tie things up. They allowed just 20 total yards on the Spartans' next two drives, and Jackson Kleather nailed the game-winning 34-yard field goal with two seconds remaining to continue Northwestern's surprise start.

23. James Madison (7-0, Previous Rank: 24)

Week 7 Result: WIN vs. Georgia State (49-22) Next Week: at Appalachian State

After surviving a 27-24 game against Georgia Southern on the road a week ago, the Dukes cruised to victory with 515 total yards and seven touchdowns against a one-loss Georgia State team that was second in the Sun Belt East Division entering play. Camden Coleman (13/19, 185 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT), George Pettaway (14 carries, 119 yards, 1 TD) and JC Evans (101 total yards, 3 TD) led the offensive onslaught.

Week 7 Result: WIN vs. Virginia (23-13) Next Week: vs. California

Kevin Jennings (23/36, 246 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT) outplayed Beau Pribula (13/22, 137 yards, 0 TD, 0 INT) in a matchup of high-profile ACC quarterbacks. The Mustangs iced the victory with an eight-play, 75-yard scoring drive in the fourth quarter, punctuated by a touchdown strike from Jennings to Jalen Hale to make it a two-possession game. It was the second straight turnover-free game for SMU as they continue to rebuild their resume following an early loss to Louisville.

21. Boise State (5-1, Previous Rank: 25)

Week 7 Result: BYE Next Week: at Washington State

A 34-27 loss to then-No. 2 Oregon in Week 1 actually helped solidify the Broncos as the team to beat in the Group of Six conversation. They have won five in a row since that opening defeat, including quality wins over Memphis and Fresno State, and they should be favored in all of their remaining games. Running back Dylan Riley (127 carries, 835 yards, 6 TD) has been the focal point of the offense, while veteran quarterback Maddux Madsen (66.3 cmp%, 1,296 yards, 13 TD, 0 INT) has done a terrific job protecting the football.

Week 7 Result: BYE Next Week: vs. Iowa State

Quarterback Noah Fifita entered Week 7 leading the Big 12 in completion percentage (73.3), passing yards (1,756), passing touchdowns (16) and passer rating (174.0), giving the Wildcats one of the most reliable signal callers in college football. The only blemish on their resume is a road loss to BYU, and they still have games against Texas Tech (Oct. 31) and Utah (Nov. 14) to further prove they belong in the national conversation.

Week 7 Result: WIN at Texas (27-24) Next Week: BYE

A roller coaster season for the Gators continues. They vaulted onto the national scene with a 52-28 victory over then-No. 4 Ole Miss during a 4-0 start, but then quickly crashed back to earth with consecutive losses to Missouri and South Carolina by a combined 47 points. Tramell Jones Jr. (22/35, 155 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT) played well in his first career start in place of an injured Aaron Philo, leading the offense to 24 straight points while flipping a 17-3 deficit to a 27-17 lead.

18. Wake Forest (5-1, Previous Rank: 21)

Week 7 Result: Winning at California (34-0, halftime) Next Week: BYE

Full details will be added after game is complete.

Week 7 Result: WIN vs. Mississippi State (31-0) Next Week: at Auburn

Sam Leavitt had his best passing game of the season, completing 31-of-38 pass attempts for 289 yards and four touchdowns. He was forced to shoulder the load offensively with the running game limited to 90 yards and 2.9 yards per carry. On defense, the Tigers had an interception and forced five turnovers on downs and two punts, though the Bulldogs were playing without star quarterback Kamario Taylor and running back Fluff Bothwell. After an up and down start, LSU can still make a statement down the stretch with games against Alabama, Texas and Tennessee still to come.

Week 7 Result: WIN vs. Oklahoma State (35-32) Next Week: at Utah

Conner Weigman threw an interception on Houston's first drive of the game, but shook it off to put together his best passing performance of the season in a solid resume booster for the Cougars. Despite the early miscue, he finished 24-of-33 passing with 343 yards and five touchdowns, and both Amare Thomas (7 catches, 126 yards, 2 TD) and Trent Walker (7 catches, 104 yards, 1 TD) had big receiving games. The Cowboys made it interesting with a pair of fourth-quarter touchdown drives, but Houston sealed the victory with a 10-play, 53-yard drive that milked the final 4:54 off the clock.

Week 7 Result: BYE Next Week: at Minnesota

With a defense that's allowing 14.5 points per game and a rushing attack piling up 194.0 yards per contest, the Hawkeyes are winning the same way they always win. Their only loss came against Ohio State, and they hung 41 points on Washington in a Week 6 road victory to flash some offensive muscle going into their bye week. They play just one ranked team the rest of the way, and it's No. 25 Northwestern, so there's a path for this team to reach the Big Ten championship game.

Week 7 Result: WIN at Oklahoma (21-13) Next Week: vs. Vanderbilt

The Wildcats trailed 13-7 entering the fourth quarter, but took the lead with an eight-play, 44-yard drive that ended in a 12-yard touchdown pass from Kenny Minchey (21/28, 158 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT) to Willie Rodriguez (5 catches, 38 yards, 2 TD). A pick-six on John Mateer's second interception of the game extended the lead, and he was picked off one more time on Oklahoma's final drive for good measure as the Wildcats had four takeaways.

Week 7 Result: LOSS at Tennessee (10-26) Next Week: vs. Texas A&M

The Crimson Tide were unable to overcome four turnovers, including two interceptions and a fumble by quarterback Keelon Russell. They were held scoreless on four second-half drives with two punts, one turnover on downs and one interception, and finished with just 201 total yards and an ugly 2-of-13 showing on third-down conversions. Now Alabama will need to navigate the final five games of the season without taking a third loss, including a road matchup with LSU on Nov. 7.

Week 7 Result: BYE Next Week: at Wisconsin

The Trojans were 6-1 for the first time since 2023, when Caleb Williams was under center in his final collegiate season, and they went 1-4 the rest of the way that year to land in the Holiday Bowl. With another established signal caller under center in Jayden Maiava (67.9 cmp%, 2,045 yards, 18 TD, 3 INT), they will look to avoid a similar second-half stumble, though matchups with Ohio State (Oct. 31) and Indiana (Nov. 14) are still on the horizon.

Week 7 Result: WIN vs. Alabama (26-10) Next Week: at South Carolina

A four-takeaway day by the defense and a workhorse performance from running back DeSean Bishop (32 carries, 159 yards, 2 TD) gave Tennessee a huge victory that immediately changes the trajectory of the SEC playoff picture. The Volunteers have a relatively easy path forward with home games against Kentucky and LSU, their toughest remaining matchups, and their defense is good enough to carry them into the College Football Playoff field.

Multiple controversial finishes and more takeaways from CFB Week 7

Week 7 Result: WIN vs. Wisconsin (17-7) Next Week: vs. Michigan State

In their first game since it was announced quarterback Nico Iamaleava would be sidelined for the rest of the season, the Bruins stepped up on defense to stay undefeated. Wisconsin's dual-threat quarterback Colton Joseph was limited to 66 passing yards, 71 rushing yards and one touchdown, and the UCLA offense ground out more than 37 minutes of time of possession. Ty Diffenbach (22/33, 264 yards, 0 TD, 1 INT) held his own in his first start, while the running game provided just enough with 120 yards and two scores.

Week 7 Result: WIN vs. Missouri (31-3) Next Week: at Texas

Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss had four total touchdowns, while running backs Kewan Lacey (16 carries, 122 yards) and Makhi Frazier (15 carries, 101 yards) led a rushing attack that piled up 268 yards and 6.8 yards per carry in a dominant showing by the Rebels. The defense bent, allowing 378 total yards, but ultimately forced seven punts and two turnovers on downs. In their five wins, they have outscored the opposition 197-91, looking like one of the nation's dominant forces outside of their lopsided loss to Florida.

Week 7 Result: WIN vs. Arizona State (53-25) Next Week: at Cincinnati

Despite fumbling on their opening drive, Texas Tech still built a 43-10 halftime lead, scoring on every subsequent offensive drive of the opening half. A staggering 260-35 advantage in rushing yardage helped the Red Raiders maintain control, and J'Koby Williams had a career-high 165 rushing yards and two touchdowns to lead the way. Not to be outdone, Will Hammond also had his best game of the season at quarterback, finishing an efficient 18-of-26 passing for 232 yards and a touchdown and zero turnovers. With no BYU game on the schedule, there's a clear path to an undefeated regular season.

Week 7 Result: LOSS at BYU (24-28) Next Week: BYE

The Fighting Irish went three-and-out following an interception on defense, then surrendered the lead by allowing a 10-play, 55-yard touchdown drive. They had 1:47 remaining to come up with their own late-game heroics, but made it as far as the BYU eight-yard line before time expired on their comeback push. It was a hard-fought loss on the road against a top-10 opponent and by no means knocks Notre Dame out of the College Football Playoff conversation, but this was a chance for them to stake their claim to the No. 1 spot in the AP poll amid a wave of other losses and they came up short.

Week 7 Result: Winning at Colorado (13-0, halftime) Next Week: vs. Houston

5. Indiana Hoosiers (6-1, Previous Rank: 4)

Week 7 Result: LOSS vs. Ohio State (15-19) Next Week: at Michigan

Josh Hoover nearly hit Nick Marsh with what could have been the game-winning touchdown strike, but the standout wide receiver stepped out of bounds on the play and the Hoosiers were dealt their first loss of the season.

It was an ugly game for the Indiana offense, as Hoover completed just 20 of 40 pass attempts, the running game produced 73 yards and 2.5 yards per carry and they lost a pair of fumbles.

Their stout defense was still enough to keep them in it, and this certainly looked like a matchup of two playoff-caliber teams.

4. Georgia Bulldogs (6-1, Previous Rank: 1)

Week 7 Result: LOSS vs. Auburn (24-27) Next Week: BYE

After Gunner Stockton fumbled with 58 seconds remaining, Auburn moved the ball 40 yards for the game-winning field goal, pulling off one of the biggest upsets of the 2026 season.

Stockton finished 22-of-34 passing for 272 yards and two touchdowns, but he also had two interceptions, and his third turnover was the dagger.

It took a 13-play, 94-yard touchdown drive to tie things up earlier in the fourth quarter, and that was the first time they had found the end zone since the first quarter.

3. Ohio State Buckeyes (6-1, Previous Rank: 6)

Week 7 Result: WIN at Indiana (19-15) Next Week: BYE

The Buckeyes survived a late injury to Julian Sayin and what could have been a game-winning touchdown pass by the Hoosiers in the final two minutes to come away with the biggest win of the season.

A 38-yard touchdown pass from Sayin to Jeremiah Smith with 12:46 remaining in the fourth quarter gave Ohio State a 19-7 lead, and that ultimately held up as the game-winning score. The defense dug in the rest of the way, though Marsh's wide open catch with his foot out of bounds would have been a tough way to lose.

Sayin was limited to 15-of-29 passing for 235 yards and two touchdowns, also throwing two interceptions to double his season total. He left the field in the fourth quarter with an arm injury after taking a sack, and returned later with his arm in a sling. A well-timed bye week will give him an opportunity to get healthy ahead of a tough road matchup with USC.

Week 7 Result: WIN vs. Notre Dame (28-24) Next Week: at UCF

With College GameDay on campus, BYU came up with one of the biggest wins in school history on Saturday night, and quarterback Bear Bachmeier did it all for the Cougars.

Along with throwing for 224 yards and a touchdown, he also had 45 rushing yards and two scores on the ground, and he even hauled in a 15-yard touchdown reception. His touchdown pass came at the end of a 10-play, 55-yard drive late in the fourth quarter that ended up being the decisive score.

Defensively, the Cougars did a great job corralling the Notre Dame rushing attack, limiting them to 3.8 yards per carry, and with more on his shoulders CJ Carr finished 27-of-49 passing without finding the end zone through the air.

1. Miami Hurricanes (6-0, Previous Rank: 3)

Week 7 Result: WIN vs. Florida State (43-35, 2 OT) Next Week: vs. Pittsburgh

It took two overtimes, 583 total yards of offense and six touchdowns for the Hurricanes to survive against a three-loss Florida State team, but the Seminoles showed up in a big way for a rivalry game and played their most complete game of the season.

Javian Mallory (13 carries, 108 yards, 2 TD) did a great job stepping in as the lead back with Mark Fletcher Jr. (16 carries, 66 yards, 1 TD) banged up, and he had a 20-yard touchdown run in the first overtime. The second saw Darian Mensah throw his third touchdown pass of the game and Malachi Toney get in on the action by throwing the two-point conversion, and the defense held to close out the win.

It was not a pretty day for the Miami defense, as Ashton Daniels threw for 298 yards and four touchdowns, and the Seminoles had 443 total yards. That won't cut it when they face off against Notre Dame in a few weeks in South Bend.

articles.title: Yahoo Top 10: After a historically chaotic college football Saturday, which team deserves top spot?
articles.summary: No college football team was safe on Saturday. Five top-10 teams bit the dust and several other contenders were pushed to the brink.
articles.body:
Multi-million dollar rosters? Historic big brands? Conference juggernauts? Brash unbeatens?

On this Saturday in college football, many of them took a tumble — some of 'em right out of our Top 10.

UGA's loss to Auburn clinched one of many stats on a somewhat historic Saturday: It was the first time in AP Top 25 history that the No. 1 team lost on the final play of a game in consecutive weeks (Texas lost to Oklahoma last week on a field goal, too), and it meant that a top-ranked team lost to an unranked opponent for a second straight week for the first time since 1990!

There are so many more such notes from this chaotic day.

For the first time in the 90-year history of the AP poll, five of the top eight teams in the country lost ( No. 5 Indiana lost to No. 4 Ohio State as well ).

For the first time since 1996, Georgia, Alabama and Texas all lost on the same day. In fact, the Tide lost back-to-back regular season games for the first time in 220 tries, and Georgia's 53-game winning streak against unranked teams fell.

Plenty more happened outside of the Top 10. Did you see that Bill Belichick is now 4-2 after UNC knocked off Duke? Northwestern — Northwestern! — is 5-1 . Lloyd Carr's other grandson (not C.J.), Tommy Carr, replaced benched Bryce Underwood to deliver Michigan its first Big Ten win this year (and send Penn State to a fourth straight defeat). And Arkansas snapped a 14-game SEC losing skid at Vanderbilt.

Coordinator Matt Patricia's defense played a nasty, smashmouth game up front. The Buckeyes only got to IU's quarterback once for a sack but they held the Hoosiers' two running backs to 70 yards and pressured Hoover enough to rattle him to a 50% completion rate. In bad news, the Buckeyes lost QB Julian Sayin for "several weeks" with a throwing arm injury. Sayin emerged from the locker room in the fourth quarter in an arm sling.

If you don't know about BYU QB Bear Bachmeier, read up! Bachmeier was responsible for every single yard on the Cougars' 10-play, 55-yard, game-winning touchdown drive and BYU's defense made a goal-line stand to end it. Bachmeier threw for 224, ran for 45 and scored four touchdowns (he caught a TD too!). BYU did it all without star running back L.J. Martin, who is sidelined with an injury.

This week: beat Florida State 43-35, 2OT

The Hurricanes survived what would have been an incredibly damaging, resume-busting loss at home to the three-win Seminoles. Miami's defense needs some work if it plans to compete against the big boys come playoff time. Did FSU exploit some issues? Ashton Daniels threw for 298 and four scores and nearly completed back-to-back Hail Mary-style passes in overtime — the latter of which was ruled an interception on a tight play that was reviewed and upheld.

The Hoosiers missed two field goals, coughed up two costly fumbles and receiver Nick Marsh failed to keep his foot in bounds on what would have been a potential game-winning touchdown catch. The Buckeyes deserve plenty of credit, as noted above, but Indiana shot itself in the proverbial foot in this one. QB Josh Hoover missed on a plethora of open targets in his worst game in an IU uniform. He completed 20 of 40 attempts.

The Bruins are the last remaining undefeated team in either the Big Ten or the SEC. Let me repeat that. UCLA is the last remaining unbeaten in the country's two juggernaut leagues. First-year coach Bob Chesney's has done wonders in Westwood. On a day when the Bruins' beast of a running back struggled — Wayne Knight had a season-low 23 yards — QB Ty Dieffenbach threw for 264 yards and UCLA's defense held Wisconsin to 214 total yards.

Who was this version of Gunner Stockton? Whatever it is, the Bulldogs don't want to see him again! Stockton threw two interceptions and lost a fumble in the final seconds as Georgia marched toward a would-be game-winning field goal. But did Kirby Smart's team deserve to win this game? The Dawgs didn't play like it for much of the affair. Auburn out-rushed them by nearly 100 yards — a shocking result for a previous top-ranked squad.

The Vols had 'em and they smoked 'em (cigars) after beating the arch-rival Crimson Tide. Tennessee's defense is the real dang deal. Jim Knowles' crew has given up more than 20 points just once and that was in garbage time during a blowout at Georgia Tech. Tennessee sacked Bama QB Keelon Russell five times and he threw two interceptions. Don't look now but Tennessee RB DeSean Bishop (159 yards on 32 carries Saturday) is putting up some Heisman-type numbers: more than 500 yards rushing and six scores the last three weeks.

The Red Raiders finally crack our rankings. Their win over Oregon State earlier this season looks better by the minute and they've beaten their last two Big 12 opponents by a combined 82-32 score. QB Will Hammond isn't necessarily making people forget about Brendan Sorsby, but Tech RB J'Koby Williams is truly carrying the load. He had 165 yards and two scores on Saturday.

The Rebels defense, finally, matched its explosive offense. Trinidad Chambliss threw for 241 yards and three touchdowns, the Rebels had two backs eclipse the 100-yard mark and Pete Golding's team converted 64% of its third downs. But how about the D? After a 75-yard opening drive, the Tigers punted on seven of their next eight drives. If Ole Miss pairs a nasty defense with Chambliss' weapons, can they win it all? Yep.

It's a tough call on what team has been most surprising this year — UCLA under Chesney or Kentucky under first-year coach Will Stein. Stein became the first first-year UK coach to start 6-1 since Alpha Brumage in 1913. That's right — Alpha. The Wildcats did it with defense in Norman, picking off much-maligned OU QB John Mateer three times and returning one for a touchdown.

Miami WR Malachi Toney finished the Hurricanes' double-overtime win over Florida State with 11 catches for 154 yards and two touchdowns. (Megan Briggs/Getty Images) (Megan Briggs via Getty Images)

articles.title: College football winners and losers: Savor the significance of Week 7's chaos, because it disappears with the 24-team playoff
articles.summary: The meaning of a chaotic day like Saturday disappears when the playoff field doubles in size next season.
articles.body:
There's usually a Saturday during the middle of every college football season where we can start to separate the contenders from the pretenders.

That did not happen in Week 7. This Saturday was the opposite of separation Saturday.

The chaos in the SEC, Notre Dame's loss to BYU and Ohio State's win over Indiana exemplified what looks to be an incredibly wide-open season as we're officially at the halfway point. If you want to reliably pick an SEC champion, good luck. You might have a better chance of being right by drawing a team name out of a hat.

Texas entered Week 6 as the No. 1 team in the country. The Longhorns then lost to archrival Oklahoma thanks to two fourth-quarter Arch Manning picks. After falling six spots to No. 7, the Longhorns went and lost to an unranked team again on Saturday, as Florida scored 24 straight to take down Texas.

It's the first time since 1961 that a No. 1 team (Texas) has lost back-to-back games to unranked opponents.

Georgia was the beneficiary of Texas' first loss, as the Bulldogs took down Alabama to move into the top spot. The win was one of the finest performances of Georgia QB Gunner Stockton's career. He positioned himself as a legitimate Heisman contender in the group of quarterbacks behind Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith.

Saturday, Stockton threw two interceptions and then fumbled away Georgia's chance to beat Auburn when he simply ran into the back of an offensive lineman and lost the ball. The Tigers recovered and then kicked a field goal as time expired for a 27-24 win .

It's the first time since 1990 that the No. 1 team in the country has been taken down by unranked opponents in consecutive weeks.

Alabama didn't bounce back, either. The Tide stayed at No. 6 after their three-point loss to Georgia and went out and played a sloppy and error-filled game against No. 14 Tennessee. The Vols kicked four field goals before they finally scored a touchdown, but those four field goals would have been enough anyway in the 26-10 win.

Every team in the SEC now has at least one conference loss, and all but four of the league's 16 teams are within a game of first place.

In the Big Ten, things don't seem nearly as fraught. Though Indiana might have retained favorite status even though it lost to Ohio State on Saturday.

The Buckeyes lost QB Julian Sayin for "several weeks" because of an apparent right arm and shoulder injury sustained on a fourth-quarter sack. Freshman Luke Fahey is in line to start in two weeks against No. 19 USC. How much will Ryan Day have to lean on the run game the rest of the season?

After Ohio State won, Georgia lost and Texas' season was pushed to the brink, Notre Dame decided to join the upset party. The No. 2 Fighting Irish lost 27-24 at No. 8 BYU as Cougars QB Bear Bachmeier rushed for two scores, threw for another and caught a TD pass.

Notre Dame was positioned to go to No. 1 with a win. Instead, the Irish had to attempt to overcome an 11-point halftime deficit before BYU went back ahead with less than two minutes to go.

With Georgia and Notre Dame losing and Ohio State losing Sayin for the foreseeable future, the No. 1 team in the AP poll will probably be Miami. All the No. 3 Hurricanes did on Saturday night was need two overtimes to beat a Florida State team that's now 3-4 and might have deserved a chance at a game-tying 2-point conversion.

Given the way the first six weeks of the season unfolded, Week 7 arrived with a lot of expectations. And it somehow exceeded them to set up a fascinating final six weeks of the season.

Savor it. Because a weekend like this isn't going to be nearly as pivotal going forward.

Saturday's games came just days after it became apparent that the 12-team College Football Playoff was going to expand to 24 teams in 2027. As college football has struggled to find the balance between making every game in the regular season relevant while also having an inclusive postseason, 12 teams seemed to strike the right balance. Especially after teams like Ohio State in 2024 and Miami in 2025 went from the first round to the title game.

But the only people clamoring for 24 teams in the postseason field were the power conference schools looking to maximize every single revenue source they can. The expanded playoff is worth millions in ESPN TV money, even when you consider that conference title games will likely disappear.

Money has always run college football. Nothing is new on that front. But there's also a cost to chasing every last dollar. And the significance of days like Saturday is going to be an upfront charge in 2027.

Here are this week's winners and losers.

Tulane: The Green Wave scored 23 second-quarter points in a 31-17 upset win over Memphis on Friday night. Tulane entered the game at 2-3 but got a pick-6 from TJ Smith as part of three interceptions of Memphis QB Marcus Stokes. Despite being .500 overall, Tulane's hopes of winning the American Conference in back-to-back seasons are very much alive after the win, and the Green Wave get UTSA at home in Week 8.

Boston College: The Eagles have now surpassed last season's win total. Boston College moved to 3-3 with a 27-21 home win over a Pitt team that badly misses QB Mason Heintschel. BC QB Mason McKenzie was 17-of-28 passing for 295 yards and two touchdowns with two interceptions. One of those TDs was a 69-yard pass to Landon Wright, as Wright had two grabs for 122 yards. A bowl is still probably out of reach for BC this season though. It has games remaining against Duke, Notre Dame and Miami.

Arkansas: The Razorbacks will not go winless in the SEC in 2026. Ryan Silverfield's bunch scored a 31-21 win at Vanderbilt on Saturday night behind two rushing TDs from Cam Settles and pick-6 by defensive back Joker Johnson. Arkansas' struggles in the SEC are well-founded at this point. The Hogs lost their first two conference games by 55 combined points before losing by seven to Tennessee in Week 6. Now they can say they're out of the basement of the SEC, as Vanderbilt remains the lone winless team in the chaotic conference.

Army QB Cale Hellums: The Army QB posted the perfect service academy stat line in the Black Knights' 56-24 win over Florida Atlantic. Hellums was 1-of-2 passing for 2 yards and rushed 25 times for 195 yards and five touchdowns as Army had 60 carries for 479 yards and eight rushing TDs as a team. The win moved Army to 3-1 in the American ahead of back-to-back trips to Tulsa and Memphis.

James Madison: The Dukes are lurking in the College Football Playoff race if Boise State slips up again. James Madison is now 7-0 after a 49-22 win over Georgia State. George Pettaway rushed for two scores, while JC Evans had a passing TD and two rushing TDs and Camden Coleman threw two touchdowns. A short week lurks with a Thursday trip to Appalachian State, before another mid-week game against Troy to conclude October. But JMU has as good a shot as anyone to run the table in the regular season.

Pat Fitzgerald: The former Northwestern coach had a great opportunity to steal a win over his former employer and alma mater. Instead, Northwestern's Jackson Kleather kicked a 34-yard field goal with two seconds left to give the Wildcats a 24-21 win . Northwestern blocked a go-ahead field goal attempt by Liam Boyd with a minute to go before driving 64 yards in eight plays for the win.

Fitzgerald was hired at Michigan State after the 2025 season and his rebuild is not progressing quickly. The Spartans are now 0-4 in Big Ten play and just 2-5 overall with a trip to No. 12 UCLA on the horizon in Week 8.

Penn State: The Nittany Lions couldn't even take advantage of two first-half interceptions by Michigan QB Bryce Underwood before he was benched for Tommy Carr. Penn State led just 3-0 at the break before losing 21-18 to the Wolverines to drop to 0-4 in Big Ten. Play. Iowa State transfer Rocco Becht's struggles continued as he tossed two more interceptions and the Nittany Lions rushed for just 65 total yards on 30 attempts.

East Carolina: The Pirates lost 30-17 at UAB on Thursday night. And that loss happened in overtime.

After UAB scored to take a 24-17 lead, ECU had a chance to send the game to a second OT or win on a 2-point conversion. Instead, Delvon Gulley intercepted Emory Williams and returned the pass 80 yards for a game-clinching pick-6. The loss dropped ECU to 3-3 as UAB went to 4-3.

Purdue: It's exceptionally hard to lose to a team that commits five turnovers, yet Purdue apparently wanted to make things complicated Friday night. Washington got its first Big Ten win of the season in West Lafayette with a 38-26 win over the Boilermakers. Backup QB Elijah Brown started in place of an injured Demond Williams and threw three interceptions while the Huskies also had two fumbles. Yet Purdue couldn't capitalize.

Maryland: It's getting incredibly difficult to see how Mike Locksley's tenure lasts much longer in College Park. The Terrapins lost 37-30 at home to Rutgers on Saturday to fall to 2-5 overall and 0-4 in the Big Ten. Rutgers outscored Maryland 24-7 in the second half and all of the Scarlet Knights' points came before Maryland scored with just over two minutes to go.

This is the same Rutgers program that fell to UMass to start the season. And Maryland is going to be an underdog in each of its final five games of the season too.

articles.title: Women's Super League: Fran Kirby 'stressed' by exit of boss Dario Vidosic
articles.summary: Former England striker Fran Kirby says the departure of Brighton head coach Dario Vidosic on the eve of the season left her feeling "stressed" and "disappointed".
articles.body:
Former England striker Fran Kirby says the departure of Brighton head coach Dario Vidosic on the eve of the season left her feeling "stressed" and "disappointed".

Vidosic guided Brighton to the club's first FA Cup final this year and finished a club-record fifth and seventh in the Women's Super League before leaving abruptly on 28 August, nine days before their opener against Arsenal.

He was replaced by Real Sociedad manager Arturo Ruiz on the same day.

"It wasn't easy when I heard," Kirby told the Women's Football Weekly podcast. "I was a bit disappointed.

"I had a really good relationship with Dario and think he's a fantastic coach that can go on and achieve amazing things with top clubs.

"But we had Arsenal coming up and hadn't had a coaching session with the new manager.

Ruiz named Brighton boss after shock Vidosic exit

Brighton lost their season curtain-raiser to the Gunners, the only game Arsenal have won so far in the WSL, and went winless through their first four league matches under Ruiz.

The 29-year-old did secure his first victory in the English top-flight before the international break, thrashing promoted Charlton 5-1.

However, this Sunday, Brighton travel to champions Manchester City, who have won all five WSL matches this season, for a game live on BBC Two (Sunday, 14:30 BST).

It is the first time the two sides have met since City won 4-0 in the FA Cup final in May.

A seven-time winner of the WSL with Chelsea, Kirby conceded 2026-27 has not been easy.

"We're under no illusions – it's been a tough start," said Kirby. "Getting the manager in so late and trying to adapt to his style of play. It's difficult when it comes so close to the start of the season.

"People say, 'Who have you got after the international break?' and it's Man City. We're trying not to think too much about it."

Manchester City v Brighton & Hove Albion

Watch full coverage and follow live text updates on BBC One, BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website

Under Vidosic, Brighton became a team seeking to dominate the ball, and during his first season in charge, they were very successful with only Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester City averaging more possession per game.

They were physical too, committing the most fouls and accruing the most yellow cards in both 2024-25 and 2025-26.

"They could soak up pressure, and then build from the back," women's football journalist Annabel Bassett from The Brighton Base said. "They would overload in midfield and then possessed a real goal threat. It all came together."

That culminated in that inaugural FA Cup final in May, where they initially played well before being overrun.

Vidosic's departure damaged hopes for further progression, although Ruiz's success in leading unfancied Real Sociedad to Champions League qualification through finishing third in Liga F last year offers encouragement.

It has been a slow start. Following that opening defeat by Arsenal, Brighton dropped points against struggling Birmingham City and Aston Villa, despite strong performances.

Two League Cup wins helped, and the nature of that commanding victory over Charlton suggests Ruiz's style is starting to take root.

"We still want to play," said Kirby, "[but] now it's more about how we harm the opposition quicker. There was an element previously where we overplayed when we could have gone forward.

"It's hard to change the mindset quickly, but we've got a great group of people.

"I'm very black and white. Tell me what you want and I'll do my best for you."

Bassett has noticed the desire for possession has become even more pronounced.

"[Ruiz] talks a lot about nullifying opponents," she said. "He likes to win the ball high and their key threats are on the flanks to open up space in the middle.

"He seems really willing to try things and the message from the club is that behind the scenes, everything is working."

For his part, Ruiz is also confident his methods are getting through.

"I'm really happy with the performances and the work we have been doing," he told BBC Sport. "We could have done better to get more points but the beginning is very difficult without previous time to build identity and clarity.

"I hope that from this Sunday we can be more solid and have more consistency and clarity with and without the ball."

Beating Charlton was important for Brighton before the pause in action, especially given hosts City are on a club-record run of 15 straight home wins.

"They're a quality side," Kirby said. "You can nullify one player but then they've got another two or three.

"But we've got quality that can harm teams. Hopefully, we can put on a good performance."

articles.title: Messi brilla con doblete y asistencia en el triunfo de Inter Miami ante Atlanta United
articles.standfirst: El argentino suma 25 goles y refuerza su condición de máximo goleador de la liga
articles.summary: El argentino suma 25 goles y refuerza su condición de máximo goleador de la liga
articles.body: En su regreso al Mercedes-Benz Stadium de Atlanta, donde este verano dio una asistencia clave en la victoria de Argentina contra Inglaterra en las semifinales del Mundial de Norteamérica, Lionel Messi dio un nuevo recital y refrendó la victoria del Inter Miami por 3-1 contra el Atlanta United con un espectacular doblete. Messi alcanzó los 25 goles en la MLS para reforzar su condición de máximo artillero de la liga estadounidense esta temporada y entregó a las Garzas del técnico Cristian González el tercer triunfo consecutivo, esta vez en un duelo de preparadores argentinos con Gerardo 'Tata' Martino. Fue Germán Berterame quien inauguró el marcador con un cabezazo al borde del descanso tras un centro del uruguayo Luis Suárez. Hubo tiempo en el 51 para un milagro del meta del Inter Miami, Dayne St. Clair, ante el paraguayo Miguel Almirón, antes de que Messi comenzara su festival anotador. El argentino anotó el 2-0 en una espectacular jugada personal en la que arrancó desde la línea del centro del campo, combinó con Berterame y llegó a regatear hasta a su propio compañero antes de definir con la zurda. Era el 56 y cuatro minutos después completó su doblete personal con una jugada parecida, con un 'eslalon' entre rivales en el área de penalti antes de fulminar al meta. En el minuto 89, el ex del Inter Miami Fafa Picault anotó el gol del honor para el Atlanta desde el punto de penalti. El Inter Miami es segundo en el Este, con 55 puntos, a once de un Nashville que domina la tabla.

articles.title: La grada del Gran Canaria se vacía, la afición silba al equipo y comienza a mirar hacia el palco
articles.standfirst: La afición de Las Palmas entona el '¡Ramírez vete ya!' tras otra sonrojante derrota
articles.summary: La afición de Las Palmas entona el ¡Ramírez vete ya! tras otra sonrojante derrota
articles.body: La derrota ante el Castellón ha hecho saltar las alarmas en Las Palmas, evidenciando el creciente distanciamiento entre el equipo y su afición. El Gran Canaria fue testigo de una noche marcada por la decepción, los silbidos y el abandono prematuro de las gradas. Apenas 15.054 espectadores acudieron al encuentro y algunos decidieron marcharse antes del descanso, después de que el conjunto amarillo encajara dos goles en los primeros 22 minutos. La afición comienza a perder la paciencia con las decisiones tomadas por el club. El descontento también se trasladó al palco. El cántico '¡Ramírez, vete ya!' volvió a escucharse después de varias temporadas de relativa tranquilidad en las gradas. La elección de Juan Manuel Rodríguez para dirigir al equipo no se ha entendido. Se cuestiona tanto el cambio en el banquillo como la planificación deportiva. La apuesta pública por Luis Helguera también está bajo el foco, especialmente por la salida de futbolistas importantes y las dudas que genera la confección de una plantilla que no ofrece garantías. El panorama deportivo agrava todavía más la situación: Las Palmas se encuentra a solo tres puntos de los puestos de descenso. Ramírez, esta semana, dejó entreabierta la puerta a la continuidad de Juan Manuel Rodríguez. Que la transitoriedad se convierta en puesto fijo no convence... y eso no gusta en la grada. Un entrenador que salió ante el Castellón con una defensa de cinco y la presencia de un Bassinga inédito hasta ahora. Entre las dudas tácticas, los resultados adversos y el creciente malestar social, el club afronta un momento delicado. Las decisiones de la directiva y la respuesta del equipo están bajo máxima vigilancia. La afición ha pasado de la preocupación a la indignación y exige respuestas inmediatas para recuperar la confianza en un proyecto que empieza a tambalearse.

articles.title: Osasuna - Racing en directo | Última hora de LALIGA EA Sports en vivo hoy
articles.summary: Banquillo de ambos equipos: Osasuna: Sergio Herrera, Rafa Fernández, Arguibide, Diego Rico, Unai Santos, Rockson, Mauro, Torró, Osambela, Kike Barja,
articles.body:
Muy buenas tardes. En algo menos de tres horas (14.00) dará comienzo en El Sadar el Osasuna-Racing , correspondiente a la novena jornada de LaLiga EA Sports . Se miden dos equipos igualados en la tabla y que, aunque están fuera de la zona de descenso, ven el peligro de cerca. Eso sí, saben que, pase lo que pase, no terminarán la jornada entre los tres últimos, lo que es un respiro. El encuentro servirá para que Jagoba Arrasate regrese al banquillo de Osasuna , y además en casa. El Sadar será una caldera para recibirle.

En Osasuna se lo pierden Herrando, Oroz y Del Castillo por lesión, mientras que en el Racing no estará Eriksson , también lesionado. Arrasate recupera a Raúl Moro y Kike Barja y parece que optará por Budimir en punta con Dubasin por detrás. José Alberto, con los jugones para surtir a Zabiri.

Osasuna afronta el partido tras sumar un punto de los últimos quince, lo que le ha costado el puesto a Ramis , mientras que el Racing lleva tres jornadas sin ganar. Se miden el juego directo del cuadro navarro ante el más combinativo de los cántabros, un choque de estilos de los que enriquece LaLiga. El Budimir vs Zabiri será uno de los duelos del partido. Seis goles lleva el croata, siete el marroquí.

El Racing se medirá por segunda jornada consecutiva a un rival que estrena entrenador, después de medirse al Valencia la pasada jornada. Venga, que arrancamos.

articles.title: El Atético mira al Sttutgart... 'rezando' por el Cuti Romero
articles.standfirst: El central pasa pruebas para conocer el alcance de sus molestias en el aductor mientras Baena lidera el ensayo de los jugadores con menos minutos
articles.summary: El central pasa pruebas para conocer el alcance de sus molestias en el aductor mientras Baena lidera el ensayo de los jugadores con menos minutos
articles.body: Sin tiempo apenas de saborear el triunfo en el RCDE Stadium que confirma al Atlético como el más firme perseguidor del Barcelona en LaLiga, los de Simeone volvieron al trabajo en la mañana de este domingo con la vista puesta en el Sttutgart, rival de Champions el próximo martes. No obstante, con el grueso de la plantilla recuperando fuerzas en el gimnasio, la gran preocupación está en la clínica donde el Cuti Romero pasa pruebas para conocer el alcance de las molestias en el aductor que le llevaron a pedir el cambio frente al Espanyol. Cabe recordar que el argentino, después de ganar el enésimo duelo pasado el cuarto de hora de la segunda parte, haría señales al banquillo de inmediato pidiendo el cambio, comenzando a encenderse las alarmas desde entonces. De ahí que una vez de vuelta a Madrid, ya en frío, el Cuti esté sometiéndose a un estudio más exhaustivo para comprobar si existe una lesión o todo se queda en una simple sobrecarga. Así, a la espera de los resultados de la resonancia que determine su estado físico, el Atlético completaría una sesión sobre el césped con Baena al frente de un grupo en el que le acompañaban Lookman (que sólo jugó 45 minutos), Mendoza (sustituto del Cuti en el 67'), Sorloth, Arnau Ortiz, Le Normand, Domínguez y Obed Vargas. El resto del plantel, tanto los titulares en Barcelona, como Julián Alvarez o Llorente, que se incorporaron en la segunda mitad, realizaron una sesión regenerativa de cara a la Champions. Una cita en la que también se espera de vuelta a Cardoso, que una vez superada la gastroenteritis que le impidió estar frente al Espanyol, trabajó en el gimnasio.

articles.title: La plantilla del Barcelona regresa de Sevilla... ¡14 horas más tarde!
articles.standfirst: Y mañana, a las 10.30, vuela a París
articles.summary: Y mañana, a las 10.30, vuela a París
articles.body: El Barcelona vivió una auténtica odisea para regresar a casa después de su partido contra el Betis. Con el calendario cada vez más apretado y una semana de máxima exigencia por delante, el conjunto azulgrana sufrió un inesperado contratiempo el sábado por la noche. Las fuertes lluvias que afectaron a Sevilla alteraron los planes de viaje de la expedición culé y obligaron al equipo a hacer noche, modificando por completo la planificación prevista para preparar el trascendental compromiso contra el PSG. El conjunto azulgrana había disputado su encuentro en La Cartuja a las 18.30 horas y tenía previsto regresar a Barcelona inmediatamente después del partido. La idea era aterrizar durante la medianoche en el aeropuerto de El Prat, descansar en casa y volver al trabajo este domingo a las 11.00 horas en la Ciudad Deportiva. Sin embargo, las condiciones meteorológicas impidieron que el desplazamiento se desarrollara según lo previsto y acabaron alterando una agenda diseñada al milímetro por Hansi Flick. La expedición azulgrana permaneció dentro del avión mientras se sucedían los retrasos provocados por la lluvia. La previsión inicial de regresar a Barcelona a última hora del sábado fue perdiendo fuerza a medida que avanzaba la noche. Finalmente, cuando se comunicó que el despegue no podría producirse hasta aproximadamente las cuatro de la madrugada, se tomó la decisión de regresar al hotel y pasar la noche en Sevilla. El contratiempo supone un nuevo quebradero de cabeza para Hansi Flick. La modificación del viaje ha obligado al cuerpo técnico a reajustar la sesión de este domingo. El equipo despegó finalmente al filo del mediodía y, una vez aterrizado en Barcelona, se desplazará directamente a las instalaciones azulgranas para realizar un entrenamiento suave de recuperación en el gimnasio. El Barcelona apenas dispondrá de unas horas en la Ciudad Condal antes de volver a hacer las maletas. La expedición azulgrana tiene previsto volar este lunes a las 10.30 horas a París, donde el martes se enfrentará al PSG.

articles.title: Bordalás: "¿Carvajal? Hasta mañana no tomaré la decisión"
articles.standfirst: El técnico azulón analizó en sala de prensa el duelo del lunes frente al Rayo Vallecano
articles.summary: El técnico azulón analizó en sala de prensa el duelo del lunes frente al Rayo Vallecano
articles.body: José Bordalás comparecía este domingo en sala de prensa con motivo del duelo de este lunes frente al Rayo Vallecano. El cuadro azulón recibe a los franjirrojos y el alicantino señaló que el duelo será “determinante” para este comienzo de Liga. Además, señaló que mañana tomará la decisión de si Carvajal va o no convocado. Cómo está el equipo: “Europa ya está olvidada. Estamos centrados en el partido de mañana contra el Rayo porque no hay que olvidar que LaLiga es lo que nos da de comer. Es un partido importantísimo. El equipo está bien, ha descansado y no hay excusas por haber jugado el jueves”. Carvajal: “Sabéis que no me gusta dar pistas. Dani viene trabajando fenomenal. Hasta mañana no tomaré la decisión y ya veréis si juega o no juega Dani. Está preparado como el resto de compañeros”. Cómo afecta jugar tres partidos en una semana: “No valen las excusas, todos sabemos las dificultades que estamos teniendo por las bajas, por número de efectivos que disponemos y número de partidos. Ahora mismo estamos centrados en el partido contra el Rayo, sabemos que es un derbi, van a venir muy motivados. Es un partido muy determinante de cara a este comienzo de campeonato, que está siendo de máxima dificultad”. Borja Mayoral: “Yo lo comenté después del partido, está claro que necesitamos a todos al máximo nivel. El jugador debe entender que tiene que estar en las mejores condiciones y ojalá Borja alcance su mejor nivel”. Mensaje: “Sabemos que es un horario difícil, siempre un lunes a las nueve, pero ellos entienden que necesitamos su apoyo. Estamos en un momento importante. El apoyo de nuestra afición es muy determinante y ojalá el lunes haya un buen ambiente y consigamos una victoria”. Esquema: “Está claro que debemos mejorar aspectos del juego, mejorar en esa faceta goleadora y la defensiva, a pesar de que no somos uno de los equipos que más goles ha recibido. Estamos cometiendo errores infantiles y graves que nos han costado puntos. A nivel ofensivo tenemos que aportar todos mucho más”. Palabras de Beñat San José: “Respetamos la opinión de los colegas. Lo que puedo decir es que el Rayo ha cambiado de entrenador, pero sigue con la base de equipo de otras temporadas, con jugadores rápidos y bien dotados. Cada entrenador le da su toque y su sello, pero el potencial del Rayo sigue siendo muy alto”. Situación del Rayo: “No suelo opinar de los problemas o cosas que ocurren en otro club. Mi deber es opinar de lo deportivo, le tengo mucho respeto al Rayo y su gente. Estamos centrados en lo deportivo y debo hablar del Rayo como equipo”. Jadon Sancho: “Entiendo que se esté hablando de posibles incorporaciones, de jugadores que están sin equipo, pero ahora mismo estamos centrados en el partido de mañana. El foco es el Rayo y sabemos que vamos a tener muchas dificultades. Entiendo que me preguntéis, no por Sancho, sino por cualquier jugador, pero estamos centrados en el partido de mañana”.

articles.title: Dejan Kulusevski to finally return to Spurs matchday squad after more than 500 days
articles.summary: Bottom-of-the-table Spurs will be missing seven players for the clash with Coventry
articles.body:
Dejan Kulusevski will return to Tottenham's matchday squad for the first time in more than 500 days for Monday's visit of Coventry , but Savio and Lucas Bergvall will be absent.

Spurs have spent the majority of this week in a warm weather training camp in Marbella, but Savio was absent after he reported a "muscular problem" on Tuesday and Bergvall is sidelined for "two weeks" with a knee issue.

Those absences along with Kulusevski's ever-improving fitness have opened the door for the Swedish playmaker to potentially play on Monday night after a serious knee injury has sidelined the attacker since the end of the 2024-25 season.

"Yes, Kulusevski on the bench. We had a meeting with the medical staff. They gave the OK and it's great news. I think it's one of the best news after Everton game last season because Deki he suffered too much. He deserves to feel emotion on the pitch," boss Roberto De Zerbi told a press conference.

"Unfortunately Savio on Tuesday… before we leave for Marbella, he felt a muscular problem. We lost him for some weeks unfortunately.

"And Lucas Bergvall because he had a problem at the beginning of the game in Manchester.

"The day after Manchester (United), Sunday, he came to (the) training ground to our medical staff. And I think two weeks (out)."

De Zerbi provided a positive update on right-back Pedro Porro, who could be available for the trip to Chelsea next Saturday.

However, bottom-of-the-table Spurs will be missing seven players for the clash with Coventry with Rodrigo Bentancur suspended for a fixture where the hosts will be desperate to end a six-match winless start to the new Premier League campaign.

"Coventry is a good team. They played a fantastic Championship last season," De Zerbi said.

"But we are Tottenham, keeping humility, keeping what you want, but we want to show to be good enough to win the games, especially if we deserve to win the games."

Kulusevski could be required to help Spurs get off the mark in the league after a torrid spell on the sidelines with a patella injury, which required a second procedure in March to fix the long-standing problem.

After Kulusevski missed Tottenham's Europa League triumph in 2025, the whole of last season and this summer's World Cup, De Zerbi was delighted to tell the 26-year-old on Saturday that he would be in the matchday squad against Coventry.

De Zerbi revealed: " I said to him, 'I spoke with the medical staff and they gave me the OK' and he smiled like this (wide).

"And we are happy. We are very, very happy. It's not football. I'm not speaking about football. OK, he's a special player, but we are speaking about different things. He suffered a lot and his reaction was great."

Richarlison remains unavailable after he was left out of Tottenham's 25-man Premier League squad following an eventful end to the summer transfer window – but featured and scored for the club's Under-21s on Tuesday in a Jersey Mike's Trophy match at Cheltenham.

On Saturday, Richarlison posted on his Instagram story "you are right" alongside a story where ex-Everton forward Duncan Ferguson criticised De Zerbi's treatment of the Brazil forward.

But De Zerbi insisted: "It's not my problem any more. You have to ask Vinai (Venkatesham), to Johan (Lange), it's not my problem."

articles.title: Manchester United commission detailed Natan reports as Barcelona open transfer talks
articles.summary: Manchester United are said to be closely monitoring Real Betis centre-back Natan, although Barcelona have moved ahead of the Red Devils by opening discussion...
articles.body:
Manchester United are said to be closely monitoring Real Betis centre-back Natan , although Barcelona have moved ahead of the Red Devils by opening discussions over a potential transfer.

How Natan emerged on Barcelona's defensive shortlist

Barcelona sporting director Deco identified Natan as a possible left-footed centre-back target in April. The defender was then offered to the Catalan club, with his agent André Cury meeting Deco in June to discuss a possible move.

On 12 August, AS stated that Barcelona remained interested but Real Betis had not received an offer. Cury said the Catalans had discussed his client with the Seville club.

Cury provided a further update later that month, saying Barcelona and Manchester City had contacted him and were seriously interested. Neither club had made a formal bid at that stage.

United commission detailed scouting reports as Barça advance

fussball-news.de now states that Barcelona have intensified their efforts, with Deco holding discussions with Cury to explore the conditions of a deal.

The outlet identifies Manchester United, Manchester City, Chelsea and Juventus as interested clubs. The Red Devils and their Premier League rivals are monitoring Natan regularly and commissioning detailed scouting reports on the 25-year-old.

United have not moved into talks, however. The publication states: "However, there are currently no concrete negotiations with the Premier League clubs."

Barcelona are targeting a left-footed defender with physical presence and quality in possession. Natan's pace, aerial strength, tackling and ability to defend space behind the back line are presented as key parts of his appeal, while the player is open to joining the Spanish champions.

Betis are asking for between €40 million and €45 million, potentially including performance-related add-ons. Natan is contracted until 30 June 2030, leaving his club in a strong position, although they would consider a sale if a sufficiently lucrative offer arrived.

From Flamengo breakthrough to a permanent home at Betis

Natan developed at Flamengo and made his senior breakthrough in 2020. He was part of the squad that won the 2020 Brazilian championship before joining RB Bragantino on loan in 2021.

The centre-back recorded 104 appearances and three goals for Bragantino. Napoli signed him permanently on 7 August 2023, and he went on to make 14 Serie A appearances, six in the Champions League and one in the Coppa Italia.

Betis recruited Natan on loan with a purchase option in August 2024. He played 52 matches and scored twice in his first season, helping the club reach the Conference League final and earning selection in UEFA's team of the season.

The Spanish side exercised their option in June 2025, paying a reported €9 million.

At the price now being discussed, United should resist being dragged into an auction before deciding that Natan is a clear upgrade rather than merely another well-scouted option. Barcelona's head start makes a patient approach particularly sensible.
